title: The R&D control plane: one registry of every result, with provenance and freshness checks
request: Make every experiment result reproducible and auditable: record where it came from, collect all results into one registry, keep known leakage off the champion boards, and refuse stale generated knowledge.
spec: dclab_rnd as a command-line control plane (python -m dclab_rnd): result normalization into knowledge/experiment_registry.csv, a knowledge base, a data-quality report and a next-experiments backlog; provenance (git commit and dirty state, Python and package versions, seed, SHA-256 of source data) in every new result; make rd-sync and make rd-check; a CI workflow that refuses stale artifacts.
plan: Write provenance.py and record.py so the shared runners stamp every new result with schema_version and provenance.
Write registry.py to normalize all historical result JSON into one ledger, flag malformed and duplicate results and benchmark regressions, and keep known leakage off the deployment leaderboards.
Generate KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md, NEXT_EXPERIMENTS.md and DATA_QUALITY.md from the registry.
Add make rd-sync, rd-check, rd-status, rd-smoke and a controlled cycle command for one runner.
Add a GitHub workflow with a daily evidence-health check.

decisions.decision: Full training stays explicit through one cycle command per runner.
decisions.why: It prevents an accidental all-model, all-dataset compute run.

decisions.decision: Exclude known leakage from the deployment leaderboards in the registry itself.
decisions.why: A champion table built from mixed safe and unsafe runs would show the leaky 0.9793 as the best HyperAck model.

decisions.decision: Generated knowledge is checked for freshness, not trusted.
decisions.why: A registry that drifts from the result files silently misleads every later reader.

change: New dclab_rnd package (cli, registry, provenance, record, analysis, report, cycle), generated knowledge files, Makefile targets and .github/workflows/rd-knowledge.yml.

findings.defect: The CI workflow installed no dependencies, so it could never pass.
findings.scenario: Found during the 2026-10-03 restructure: the workflow ran the checks on a bare runner, where importing the package's dependencies fails before any check runs.
findings.cause: No requirements file for CI existed.
findings.fix: Add requirements-ci.txt with only the packages the automation layer needs and install it in the workflow; the restructure was then checked in a clean environment with only those packages.
findings.test: The restructure commit's checks (22 unit tests, record validation, knowledge freshness, campaign verification) passed in a clean CI-only environment.
findings.impact: Every run of the workflow failed at import before any check, so stale knowledge or a malformed result would never have been caught by CI, while the workflow's presence suggested it would be.
alternatives: Install the full research environment in CI: set aside for a small CI-only requirements file, because the checks validate and rebuild records and never train a model.

findings.defect: The CLI imported the OpenAI client at module level, so validate and sync failed without it.
findings.scenario: On a machine without the openai package, python -m dclab_rnd validate stopped at import, though validation needs no model.
findings.fix: Import the OpenAI client lazily, only in the commands that call a model.
findings.test: validate, sync and campaign verify run in the CI environment, which has no openai package.
findings.impact: On any machine or runner without openai, validate, sync and campaign verify stopped at import, so the checks that need no model could not run at all; it was one reason the CI job could not pass.
alternatives: Make openai a required dependency: set aside because validation, sync and verification never call a model.

findings.defect: The committed experiment registry was stale on 10 rows.
findings.scenario: sync --check failed on the restructure branch because ten registry rows no longer matched their result files.
findings.cause: Results had been added without rerunning rd-sync.
findings.fix: Regenerate the registry; rd-check keeps failing while any generated file is stale.
findings.test: python -m dclab_rnd sync --check is part of make rd-check.
findings.impact: Ten rows of the committed ledger disagreed with their result files, so a reader of the registry, or of a champion board built from it, saw numbers that no result file held.

outcome: Every historical result (579 records) sits in one ledger with provenance for new runs; the champion boards exclude known leakage; stale knowledge fails the check. This is the plumbing every later campaign, the evidence index and the SFT builders read.
lessons: A check that cannot run (a CI job with nothing installed) is worse than none, because it looks like protection.
Optional dependencies must be imported where they are used, or the light commands inherit the heavy ones' failures.
risks: A champion board built from mixed safe and unsafe runs, crowning the leaky HyperAck model.
A registry that drifts from the result files and silently misleads every later reader.
One command that launches training for every model on every dataset by accident.
Provenance without the dirty state or the data hash, so a result cannot be traced to the code and data that made it.
A CI check that cannot actually run and only looks like protection.
